title: Extreme-poverty summary (real CC-BY prose from Our World in Data)

source.attribution: Our World in Data (Roser, Hasell, et al.), CC-BY-4.0
source.notes: Prose is composed from real, verbatim Our World in Data sentences (CC-BY) arranged into a short excerpt: 1990 = 2.3 billion / 44%; 2025 = ~800 million / one in ten / $3 line; >1.5 billion fewer than 1990; 24% under $5/day, 52% under $10/day. Clean version verified internally consistent (2.3B - 0.8B = 1.5B decline; <$5 share <= <$10 share) before injecting 3 self-contained defects. OWID is a living article; source_ref pins the retrieval date.

construction.proposer: opus-4.8 (proposed); audited & confirmed 2026-07-05 via oracle audit (validator + anchor-resolution + real/findable/unique pass, docs/oracle-audit-2026-07-05.md) with a targeted human audit of ambiguous/interacting defects and all gray zones (docs/human-audit-checklist)

clean_regions.note: the 2.3 billion (1990) figure is the real, untouched value
the ~800 million (2025) figure is the real, untouched value
the 52% under $10/day figure is real and untouched

known_gray_zone.note: The extreme-poverty line is stated as $3/day (OWID's updated line). A reviewer relying on outside knowledge of a different line (e.g. $2.15) might flag it; that is not a seeded defect, so exclude from false-finding scoring.
